status_note: Ran 2026-08-20 on av2 and av3 through the campaign queue. FRETISH phase 14:50:22 to 15:10:06, TLSF phase 15:10:10 to 17:04:00, by the hosts' own clocks; av3 runs ~17 min fast with NTP off. Collected and closed the same day. The TLSF half was first collected mid-run at 417 of 480 rows and topped up to 480 at close; the merge verified as a union with no duplicate keys.
kind: repair campaign (FRETISH + TLSF), two-arm, paired, pre-registered
kind_note: Sweep O at two levels, opslegacy and opsfixed, paired on (spec, seed), both arms of a pair on the same host so a host difference cancels inside the pair. One binary serves both arms through [genetic] repaired_operators, because campaign.py stages one branch per campaign and commit may never join KEY_FIELDS, so two binaries would collide on the merge key.
question: Whether the seven mutation and crossover grammar repairs of 2026-08-19, audited in experiments/2026-08-14-aurus-h2h/REPORT.md, improve repair quality over the grammar every archived campaign ran. PLAN.md in this directory is the pre-registration, fixed before any row was collected.
endpoint: Paired per-run implies_ideal, exact McNemar over the discordant pairs, per path, never pooled.

fret.verdict: no significant difference; fails its own wall-ratio bound independently

tlsf.verdict: opsfixed wins at p < 0.05 and holds its own wall-ratio bound

result.timed_out_note: Zero on both arms and both paths, so the pilot-sized caps held and the directional censoring PLAN.md section 8 registered did not occur.
result.per_spec_note: The TLSF result is carried by minepump, which goes 0/20 under opslegacy to 12/20 under opsfixed (12 discordant pairs, none the other way). codesample-un2 adds 4-0 and humanoid-531 runs the other way at 3-8. On FRETISH the whole effect is fsm at 9-1; fsm-timing and takeoff are 30/30 in both arms. The plan registered no per-spec test and these are exploratory.

decision_rule_firing: Outcome 1 as written: the repaired arm wins the primary endpoint on TLSF at p < 0.05, loses neither path significantly, and the winning path's median paired wall ratio is 1.230, under the 1.25 bound that amendment 9a fixed as per path. FRETISH fails both conjuncts independently and does not gate TLSF under 9a.
decision: Superseded on its own plan's terms, and then overtaken by a wider decision. PLAN.md section 8 pre-registered, before any row was collected, that this campaign is run with the weakening screen held on, that the screen's default is going to false, and that 'this campaign's result must not be read as predicting the comparison under the new default; that is a separate replication, and it is the one that decides what ships'. That replication is 2026-08-20-ops-weakening, which returned a null on both paths. On 2026-08-20 the maintainer nonetheless made the repaired grammar permanent -- genetic.repaired_operators removed rather than defaulted, both legacy code paths deleted -- and flipped run_weakening_filter to false in the same change. That decision rests on this campaign's outcome-1 firing under the screen-on configuration, on minepump's 0/20 to 12/20 reachability result, and on the 2026-08-14 audit, rather than on the pooled endpoint under the shipping configuration, which is null. It is recorded here as a maintainer decision, not as the pre-registered rule firing under the configuration the rule was meant to bind.
decision_caveat: The 2x2 in ops-weakening's PROVENANCE.json is what qualifies the outcome-1 firing: dropping the weakening screen lifts the OPSLEGACY arm by 19 TLSF runs and 9 FRETISH runs, both strictly one-way, against 6 and 4 for opsfixed. The grammar repairs and the screen removal recover substantially the same repairs, so the +13 TLSF grammar effect measured here falls to 0 once the screen is off. Reading this campaign's p = 0.047 as the effect of the repairs under the configuration counter now ships would overstate it.

profile_commit.held_by_tag_note:
LOAD-BEARING, AND UNDER THE NEVER-DELETE RULE. The branch fix/mutation-operators was squashed on 2026-08-20, so d730c27, 201d925 and 09a5eb8 are not ancestors of the history that reaches main and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 201d925 main` will not succeed. The annotated tag provenance/mutation-operators, together with the campaign/ops-weakening branch, is what keeps them and every blob sha this file names resolvable against git gc. Push the tag and do not delete it; this is the position 2026-07-31-replicate and the TLSF branch are in.

What the squash does NOT cost is the substantive claim, because this file does not rest on the shas alone. `engine_tree` above names the compiled source by content, and those tree ids are identical across all three commits and are carried by the archival commit itself, which sits before the commit that removed genetic.repaired_operators and rewrote src/ and include/. So 'this binary was built from this source' stays verifiable from main's own history even if every sha below stops resolving. The shas remain recorded because they are what the binaries reported -- 720 rows carry them in the CSV `commit` column -- and are data about the run rather than pointers this archive depends on.
profile_commit.reachable_from_main_note: False and expected to stay false: the branch was squashed rather than merged, so the content reaches main under a fresh sha. Verify the engine instead of the commit, with `git rev-parse <commit>:src` against the engine_tree ids above.

merge_disposition.why: Chosen deliberately once engine_tree made the provenance claim content-addressed rather than sha-addressed. The ordering constraint the squash had to respect is that the archival commit stays separate from, and before, the commit removing genetic.repaired_operators, so that a commit carrying the campaigns' engine tree remains reachable from main.

profile_commit_evidence: Both hosts were staged through campaign.py, which fetches the pushed commit, checks it out, rebuilds and reads counter --version back before anything launches. Each per-host manifest records git.head and both binaries at that commit with dirty 0. --allow-stale-binary was never passed to a run that produced a retained row.

engine_tree.note:
The engine the campaign ran, named by content rather than by commit. These git tree and blob ids are identical across all three of d730c27 (ops-pilot), 201d925 (ops-grammar) and 09a5eb8 (ops-weakening): the commits differ only under experiments/ and scripts/, so one compiled source tree produced every binary in all three campaigns, and the binaries differ from each other solely in the version string cmake/version.cmake bakes in. Verify with `git rev-parse <commit>:src` and so on.

This is the durable half of the provenance and it is why the recorded commit shas may be rewritten. A squash or rebase replays content under fresh shas, but a tree id is content-addressed and does not move, so the claim 'this binary was built from this source' survives intact provided some commit reachable from main still carries these ids. The one requirement a rewrite must respect is therefore that the archival commits stay SEPARATE from, and ordered before, the commit that removed genetic.repaired_operators -- that removal changes src/ and include/, so a history in which it is squashed together with the archive leaves no commit carrying the tree these campaigns ran, and the ids below would name objects git gc collects. Kept apart, the tag provenance/mutation-operators is redundant and may be deleted.

binary_commit.source: counter --version, captured on both hosts into the per-host manifests after the pre-launch rebuild

rows.endpoint_note: FRETISH 4 specs x 2 arms x 30 seeds = 240; TLSF 12 specs x 2 arms x 20 seeds = 480. Every row is an endpoint observation and every (spec, seed) case is fully paired -- 120 FRETISH pairs and 240 TLSF pairs, no unpaired case on either path.
rows.seeds: FRETISH 0-29, av2 0-14 and av3 15-29; TLSF 0-19, av2 0-9 and av3 10-19; disjoint on both

uncontrolled: Three simplifier folds landed with the repairs and are not behind the key: G G phi -> G phi, F F phi -> F phi, and the U/W/R self-join folds in src/prop_formula/simplify.cpp. They are semantics-preserving and Formula::simplify() has no config access, so they ship in both arms. The campaign therefore measures the repairs GIVEN the folds, and the control arm is not main's prior behaviour but the behaviour counter would ship with the key left false. PLAN.md section 4 is the record, written before the run.

vendored_scripts.note: The analysis of record is scripts/analyse_ops.py in this directory. It is post hoc -- written at the close, from PLAN.md rather than committed with it -- and scores this campaign and ops-weakening together, because the 2x2 needs both.

known_caveats: Sweep O and the ops-fret / ops-tlsf profiles are retired: their two arms were the two grammars, and genetic.repaired_operators was removed on 2026-08-20. Neither this campaign's configs nor ops-weakening's run against a current binary -- every one of them sets a key the binary now rejects. Reproduce at 201d925 through the vendored scripts/. This is the same position [filters.intervals] left 2026-08-06-wellsep-timing and TLSF sweep V in.

run_weakening_filter defaulted true when this ran and is false from 2026-08-20. Both arms state run_weakening = true explicitly in their emitted configs, so nothing here is silently reinterpreted by that flip; the archived configs mean what they say.
Frozen ideals bias implies_ideal across incomparable families, but both arms score against the same ideals, so the bias is common-mode and cancels inside the pairing.
The FRETISH corpus is 4 families and two of them (fsm-timing, takeoff) are 30/30 in both arms, so the path's whole resolving power sits on fsm and fsm-combined.
